status: registered before any GSE135834 data file was downloaded or opened by this program. The three other cohorts' tracks were downloaded under earlier registrations of this program (disclosed below); the pooled statistics defined here have never been computed. Read before registration: GEO metadata (series and sample SOFT/matrix for GSE135834, the FTP directory listing, and HTTP response headers of the 6 listed files confirming names and Content-Length, no data bytes) and literature (design/prior-art-libvar.md)
origin: Registered placebos in this program's earlier tests repeatedly showed GC-correlated differences between same-condition libraries: RPE1 SunTag WT pair rho +0.61 (lbr/), MEF between-embryo WT pairs -0.13 to -0.27 (mef/), K562 WT pairs -0.06/+0.04 (damid/). These gradients decided two registered labels (lbr/ and mef/ both DIRECTION_ONLY) and downgraded the GC-lamina candidate. This study quantifies the phenomenon itself across cohorts, with a never-opened cohort as holdout.
hypothesis: pairs of same-condition lamina DamID/pA-DamID libraries differ by systematic GC-correlated gradients of a magnitude comparable to a substantial fraction of canonical lamin-perturbation contrasts, and the gradients persist after per-track z-scoring (so they are not explained by dynamic-range compression alone). Consequence: a GC-vs-lamina association from a two-library contrast is not identifiable without within-cohort same-condition calibration or an explicit GC-conditioned model

test_per_pair: delta = track_a - track_b in the listed order; baseline = mean(track_a, track_b); code/screen.py test_pair: rank-partial Spearman of gc vs delta, covariates tss_count and baseline (both ranked); within-chromosome circular shift of gc, 5000 shifts, one-sided p each direction; all autosomes of the cohort's build; seed 20262701 + pair index (raw arm), 20262801 + pair index (scale_free arm), 20262901 + pair index (reported-only cross-condition pairs, raw arm only)

arms.scale_free: each tile track z-scored over its finite autosomal tiles before differencing and averaging; persistence in this arm means the gradient is not a dynamic-range artifact

abort_rule: any cohort failing its genome-build check, any missing file or hash mismatch against the earlier intake receipts, or any registered pair test with n < 3000 or non-finite rho aborts with no label

registered_predictions.P1_existence: at least 60% of the 22 registered same-condition pairs have |rho_raw| >= 0.10
registered_predictions.P2_persistence: over pairs with |rho_raw| >= 0.05 (at least 4 required), median(|rho_scale_free| / |rho_raw|) >= 0.5
registered_predictions.P3_benchmark: median |rho_raw| over the 22 pairs >= 0.083, i.e. one third of 0.249, the median |rho| of the seven previously registered treatment contrasts (-0.236, -0.249, -0.272, +0.149, +0.136, -0.346, -0.348; constants frozen here)
registered_predictions.P4_holdout: in the opc cohort (never opened), at least 4 of 6 same-condition pairs have |rho_raw| >= 0.05

labels.SYSTEMATIC: P1 and P2 and P3 and P4 all pass
labels.PARTIAL: P1 and P2 and P3 pass but P4 fails (the pooled phenomenon holds; the holdout cohort does not show it at the registered bar)

no_spin: the first sentence of the outcome record reports the label and the observed pooled statistics whatever they are
diagnostics_reported: per track: autosomal tile SD and finite-tile count; per pair: sd ratio (larger/smaller), OLS slope of delta on baseline; per cohort: median |rho_raw| and pair count; for every pair both arms' rho, n, both one-sided p values; cross-condition opc pairs (reported only); count of pairs whose raw rho was previously computed under an earlier registration
prior_computation_disclosure: 7 of the 22 registered pair contrasts were previously computed under earlier registrations (identical or sign-flipped deltas): LV_mef_wt_15_18 (-0.182), LV_mef_wt_15_x17 (+0.230), LV_mef_wt_18_x17 (+0.234) [mef/ placebos], LV_rpe1_wt_sc (+0.130) [lbr/ PL_batch], LV_rpe1_cal (+0.610) [lbr/ PL_st], LV_k562_wt_r1r2 and LV_k562_wt_r1r8 [damid/ placebos, |rho| 0.061 and 0.035]. Their scale_free-arm values were likewise computed for the same pairs. These observed values motivate this study; the pooled statistics, 15 uncomputed pair contrasts, and all opc pairs are uncomputed at registration. The thresholds do not let the 7 known pairs alone decide any prediction: if all 15 uncomputed pairs were below 0.10, P1 would fail (7/22 < 60%). Caveat: baseline = mean(A,B) here, vs independent third-track baselines in the earlier registrations, so the 7 disclosed values will not reproduce exactly.
disclosed_limits: same-condition pairs across different embryos/batches/experiments also carry biological replicate variation, which makes the measurement conservative (larger) for a pure library-effect claim; pairs are not statistically independent — one anomalous library can supply several pairs (e.g. WT_x17 in two mef pairs, the three k562 WT tracks in three pairs, the opc trios) — so '60% of pairs' is a pair-level measurement, not a count of independent libraries; the opc tracks are quantile-normalized by the depositor (a stronger normalization than the other cohorts); different tile covariates (gc5Base vs 2bit-derived gc) across builds; assays differ (DamID-seq vs pA-DamID) and the study deliberately pools them as 'public lamina DamID-family tracks'
claim_ceiling: SYSTEMATIC supports: GC-correlated between-library gradients in public DamID-family lamina tracks are systematic, mostly survive z-scoring, reach at least a third of canonical lamin-perturbation effect sizes, and appear in a cohort this program had never opened. It does NOT support: a mechanism for the bias, a claim that every dataset has it, or any judgment about any specific published result beyond the cohorts tested. Prior-art status (design/prior-art-libvar.md): PARTIALLY_KNOWN - GC bias in sequencing counts and DamID normalization practice are documented (CQN; Daim; z-scoring in van Schaik 2022), but no DamID-specific quantification of same-condition GC gradients or placebo-calibration practice was found
